A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MM-DIA research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including the additional table page in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset statistics, annotation validation, speech and video generation experiments, human evaluations, and buffer-mechanism ablations in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations in Section 5 and Appendix A, including model comparisons, human ratings, and annotation-pipeline validation.

M1.justification: The data-curation pipeline, annotation procedures, Dia adapter, and Higgs fine-tuning approach remain unchanged. The redesigned Figure 2 illustrates the existing procedure rather than establishing a method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 54,700-dialogue MM-DIA dataset, 309-dialogue benchmark, three generation tasks, and daily-conversation OOD coverage. The appended dataset comparisons do not introduce datasets actually used in new experiments.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including Dia and Higgs variants, HarmoniVox, both VLM-plus-Higgs cascades, and all six video-generation systems. v2 Table 15 repeats the comparator set already evaluated in Table 6.

E3.justification: The 90:5:5 split, 598-clip Hard set, 60-clip OOD set, 133-dialogue cross-modal evaluations, metrics, and human-evaluation procedures are unchanged. The added tables introduce no new evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix A retains the same subtitle-alignment cases, annotation-quality evaluations, buffer-size ablation, and Hard/OOD analyses. The additional tables do not supply new robustness tests, ablations, or case studies.

E5.justification: Table 4 retains the same Human-MOS uncertainty reporting, and the participant and sample counts are unchanged. Neither version adds different seed information, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Matched dataset statistics, experimental scores, rankings, and findings are unchanged. v2 Table 15 reproduces Table 6's results exactly; Tables 14 and 16 reuse existing dataset counts rather than reporting new experimental outcomes.

T1.justification: The conditional-generation formulations in Section 4, keyframe-pool update in Appendix A.2, and F1 Overlap definition in Appendix A.3 are unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning MM-DIA, its annotation pipeline, the benchmark, improved explicit controllability, and limitations of implicit cross-modal control.

C2.justification: The interpretations of the controllability–timbre tradeoff, cross-modal alignment failures, video-generation limitations, and Hard/OOD behavior remain unchanged. The media-bias qualification is also retained.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, model specifications, appendix pseudocode, and code/data access statements remain unchanged. Figure 2 reorganizes existing information; the expanded computing-center acknowledgement supplies no additional hardware or experimental configuration.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work prose are unchanged, but new Table 16 extends the dataset positioning with source and segmentation comparisons, including semantic segmentation for OpenDialogue and timestamp segmentation for OpenViDial 2.0.

P1.justification: Acknowledgements add Beijing Natural Science Foundation and Tsinghua computing-center support. Cross-references change from Tables 1 and 6 to appended Tables 16 and 15. The substantive prose and section sequence remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn into numbered workflow stages. v2 appends Tables 14–16: a reduced dataset comparison, a duplicate of the video-results table, and a comparison adding source/segmentation columns. Existing tables remain, with associated page reflow.

improvement.justification: The methods, evidence, claims, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. Figure 2 reorganizes the workflow, and Table 16 provides useful comparison detail, but Tables 14 and 15 duplicate retained material. These modest clarity gains and added redundancy leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
